expected_before.notes: Traditional biography identifies Sun Wu (Sun Tzu) as a general serving King Helü of Wu and associates him with Wu's victory over Chu at Boju in 506 BCE. Modern scholarship substantially disputes whether the biographical Sun Wu existed and whether the Art of War belongs to the Spring and Autumn period. ATLAS therefore records only the traditional 506 BCE military association, marks Person historicity and Activity confidence disputed, and does not fabricate a longer career interval. This request deliberately reuses the existing Spring-and-Autumn polity Wu / 오나라 already represented by King Helü (514–496 BCE); it is distinct from the later Three Kingdoms polity Eastern Wu / 동오.

expected_after.notes: Traditional biography identifies Sun Wu (Sun Tzu) as a general serving King Helü of Wu and associates him with Wu's victory over Chu at Boju in 506 BCE. The biographical tradition and the dating/authorship of the Art of War remain debated. ATLAS keeps Sun Wu in the historical Person table, records only the representative c.506 BCE military association, retains Activity confidence as disputed, and does not fabricate a longer career interval. This Activity reuses the Spring-and-Autumn polity Wu / 오나라 already represented by King Helü (514–496 BCE); it is distinct from the later Three Kingdoms polity Eastern Wu / 동오.
